title: The Hitopadesha
author: narayana
attributionNote: Ascribed to a Narayana, of whom nothing further is known. He drew the stories from the Panchatantra and the Mahabharata and arranged them as a course of instruction for a prince.
description: A teacher, Vishnusharman, undertakes to educate three princes who learn nothing from books, and does it with stories: the loss of friends, the winning of friends, war and peace. A crow, a turtle, a lion, a jackal and a louse argue out trust, flattery, counsel and the limits of cleverness, each tale closing in a verse that states the lesson.
historicalContext: The Sanskrit version of the animal fables of the Panchatantra, and the one that travelled: it was translated into Persian for the Mughal court and thence into European languages, and it is the form in which the Indian beast fable reached the West.
availabilityNote: Complete: all four books and 715 verses of the GRETIL e-text, with the opening verses of the author's salutation, which the source numbers 0.x, dropped as the file's own preface rather than part of the work. Streamed one book at a time; the prose framing is carried with the verse that closes each story.
